guarantees.claim: On asynchronous reset (negedge rst_ni) or when timer_update is high at posedge clk_i, timer_expired is set to 1'b0.
When timer_enable is high and timer_value equals all zeros at posedge clk_i, timer_expired is set to 1'b1.
When none of the above conditions are true, timer_expired holds its previous value.

assumptions.claim: External logic must assert timer_update to clear timer_expired after the timer expires; otherwise timer_expired remains asserted indefinitely.
assumptions.risk: Repeated consumption of the same expiration event, leading to over-sampling of entropy or protocol deadlock.

uncertain_points.claim: The compile‑time context indicates a generate if (!rst_ni) guard, suggesting the always_ff block may be conditionally instantiated by a parameter named rst_ni, while the block itself uses rst_ni as an active‑low reset signal. This conflict must be verified.
uncertain_points.cond: If the generate condition is parameter‑based and the parameter equals 1
uncertain_points.risk: The whole block would be omitted, leaving timer_expired undriven (potentially X), breaking downstream entropy/security logic.

uncertain_points.claim: timer_expired is only set on (timer_enable && timer_value == 0) and is not automatically cleared when timer_value becomes non‑zero while enabled. If the timer is restarted without an explicit timer_update, the expired flag remains asserted, falsely indicating expiration.
uncertain_points.cond: timer_value transitions from 0 to non‑zero while timer_enable = 1 and timer_update = 0
uncertain_points.risk: Spurious expiration signal may cause incorrect entropy sampling or state‑machine errors.
